newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Asia Gas Oil/Jet - Diesel again tests $25-support.
newsitem.headline: Asia Gas Oil/Jet - Diesel again tests $25-support.

text.p: Singapore gas oil prices are again poised to test the strong support of $25.00 per barrel as a glut in the MidEast and Asia are causing jitters despite strong crude values, traders said on Thursday.

"There is a very good likelihood that prices would break the $25.00-support soon," one trader said. "The West is very strong on crudes which is now providing the support, but if that turned around, it would cause problems to the (diesel) market."

Traders said that overall there is a lot of pressure on the market as there are a lot of barrels in the MidEast and Singapore. Stocks in Singapore for the week ended May 21 was 10.345 million barrels, at least a three-year high, the Trade Development Board said.

Additional pressure were seen from China's lack of appetite to take more cargoes amid brimming storage on the mainland as well as in Hong Kong, with ships continuing to line up to discharge cargoes off the Fujian port of Xiamen.
Traders said that if China's state refiner SINOPEC finally decided to reduce ex-refinery gas oil prices by 100 yuan per tonne from 2,190 yuan, the prospect of more imports would be dimmer.
In the physical market, two refiners in Singapore were actively offering with three cargoes seen traded at 15-25 cents below the $25.35-level done on Tuesday, traders said.

A European refiner sold a cargo to a Singapore trader at $25.10 per barrel for June 17-21 lifting free-on-board (fob) basis. A Japanese trader bought two cargoes--at $25.20 for June 6-10 lifting from a Swiss trader and at $25.20 for June 17-21
from another European major.
The Singapore swaps jet fuel/gas oil spread continued to be under pressure as the bearish tone were more serious for jet fuel because refiners have a lot of jet to sell, traders said.
June regrade was last quoted at minus 30 and minus 15 cents.
Physical jet fuel was offered slightly lower with three offers seen at $24.50 and $24.55 per barrel for mid-and-second-half June lifting fob. Nothing was traded.
India has issued a tender to buy kerosene for July deliveries, which will close on June 5. India cancelled its last tender for June delivery and bought two cargoes for May.
